title: Preise, Euro und Telefonnummern
summary: Hundreds and thousands, euro prices, and how Germans read phone numbers aloud

blocks.title: Große Zahlen: hundert & tausend
blocks.body: **hundert** (100) and **tausend** (1000) just glue onto the front of a number: 200 = *zweihundert*, 300 = *dreihundert*, 2000 = *zweitausend*. Big numbers stay **one word**, however long: 150 = *hundertfünfzig*. You'll rarely need more than a few hundred day-to-day — Bäckerei prices, rent, phone numbers.

blocks.title: Preise: Euro und Cent
blocks.body: Money talk: **der Euro**, **der Cent**. Ask a price with *Wie viel kostet das?* ("How much does that cost?") and answer with *Das kostet …* or *Das macht …* ("that comes to…"). Euro and Cent don't change in the plural after a number — *zwei Euro*, not *zwei Euros*.
blocks.callout: 3,50 € is said *drei Euro fünfzig* — just like English "three fifty", drop the word Cent.

pairs.note: German uses a **comma** where English uses a period for the decimal — read *3,50* as *drei Euro fünfzig*, never "three comma five zero".
For thousands, German flips it again: a **period** (or a space) marks the thousands, not a comma.

blocks.prompt: How do you say €7.30 in German?
blocks.explain: Say the euros, then the cents as a plain number — no "Cent" needed, just like English "seven thirty".

blocks.prompt: Type the German for 'That costs four euros twenty.'
blocks.explain: Das kostet vier Euro zwanzig — no comma word, no "Cent", just run the numbers together.

lines.en: Zero one five one… (mobiles start with 0)
I say the numbers one by one.

blocks.scene: Lena buys breakfast at the Bäckerei and you get her number to meet again.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.target: So, zwei Brötchen und ein Kaffee — das macht drei Euro zwanzig.
lines.en: So, two rolls and a coffee — that comes to three twenty.
lines.spotlight: *Das macht …* is how you hear a total at the counter.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Perfekt, danke! Sag, wie ist deine Telefonnummer?
lines.en: Perfect, thanks! Hey, what's your phone number?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.target: Klar! Null eins fünf eins, zwei drei vier, fünf sechs sieben acht.

questions.q: What does the breakfast order come to?
